newsitem.title: CHINA: China envoy in HK sees better ties with Britain.
newsitem.headline: China envoy in HK sees better ties with Britain.

text.p: A top Chinese diplomat voiced the hope on Friday that China and Britain could patch up relations that had become strained before Hong Kong's return to China one month ago.

Ma Yuzhen, the Hong Kong commissioner of China's Foreign Ministry, said Britain's return of the former colony "could provide us with new opportunities for further developing good relations between the two countries."

Ma's remarks to Hong Kong government radio followed comments earlier this week by Britain's minister responsible for Hong Kong affairs, Derek Fatchett, who said it was time to put aside the past and look to the future.
Britain handed Hong Kong backed to China on July 1, ending 156 years of colonial rule. But a bitter quarrel over electoral reforms had put the two countries at odds for several years.

Ma said, "In order to make sure the Sino-British relations continue to develop in the right direction...I think it is important that our relations are guided by the principle of mutual respect, dealing with each other on equal footing and not interfering in each others' internal affairs."
Hong Kong's financial markets continued to show confidence in the territory under Chinese rule.
Stocks finished the Friday morning session slightly higher, lifted chiefly by buying in the property developers and despite profit-taking in the banks, brokers said.
But just a month after China took over the former British colony, the new government is grappling with discontent over its proposed arrangements for next May's Legislative Council polls.
The pro-democracy camp and human rights activists have condemned the draft rules as unfair and tantamount to a rollback of democracy, and said it would provoke legal challenges.

Political parties in Hong Kong, including some usually pro-Beijing in stance, urged new leader Tung Chee-hwa's government in a series of consultation papers to widen the franchise in the 30 so-called functional constituencies that are based on business sectors.

The post-colonial government received more than 200 papers after a nine-day pulsetaking exercise to tap public views on its electoral plan, which will give votes to corporations rather than individuals to elect legislators from the functional constituencies.
Meanwhile, China's People's Liberation Army garrison in Hong Kong celebrated the PLA's 70th birthday on Friday and was attempting to improve its image with the community.
The PLA garrison opened some bases to select visitors over the past week.
Hong Kong's government is holding talks with the PLA on details of implementing China's Hong Kong Garrison Law, which allows the PLA to pass through frontier posts without customs inspections.
Concerns have been raised the troops may get involved in cross-border smuggling.
